hops.rationale: The accumulated AAPL FY2023 evidence (filing 000032019323000106) directly states the requested dependence on third-party manufacturing and supply-chain risk. Passage 22 says much of manufacturing is outsourced to partners in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam, often at single locations, and that outsourcing reduces direct control. Passage 23 says the company relies on single-source outsourcing partners for components and on Asia-based partners for final assembly of substantially all hardware, and describes disruption risks and supply/pricing risk from single or limited sources. Passage 24 covers component shortages, supplier financial distress, and custom single-source components. Passage 18 adds single or limited sourcing and supplier industrial-accident risk. Passage 49 is about receivables from outsourcing partners and is only marginally relevant. No requested element is missing. Filing scope is respected: no NVDA or other-company content was used.

hops.query: third-party manufacturing suppliers dependence supply chain risk
hops.requested_goal: find the disclosed dependence on third-party manufacturing and supply-chain risks
hops.rationale: NVDA 2024 passages directly state the requested dependence on third-party manufacturing and supply-chain risk. Passage 000041 says NVIDIA uses third parties to manufacture and assemble products, has long lead times, and gets no guaranteed wafer, component, or capacity supply. Passage 000049 says dependence on third-party suppliers reduces control over quantity, quality, yields, and delivery, and names foundry wafer reliance and independent subcontractors. Passage 000054 adds supplier non-delivery and insolvency risks. Passage 000058 covers third-party supply-chain attacks. Passage 000035 is the risk-factor summary introducing the topic. Together they cover the core requested fact. The AAPL comparison is outside this subquery and was not graded.

We are not provided guaranteed wafer, component and capacity supply, and our supply deliveries and production may be non-linear within a quarter or year. Additionally, we depend on developers, customers and other third parties to build, enhance, and maintain accelerated computing applications that leverage our platforms. We also rely on third-party content providers and publishers to make their content available on our platforms, such as GeForce NOW. Failure by developers, customers, and other third parties to build, enhance, and maintain applications that leverage our platforms, or failure by third-party content providers or publishers to make their content available on reasonable terms or at all for use by our customers or end users on our platforms, could adversely affect customer demand. Dependency on third-party suppliers and their technology to manufacture, assemble, test, or package our products reduces our control over product quantity and quality, manufacturing yields, and product delivery schedules and could harm our business.
